brief: #109 re-keyed the early risers onto sunUp and the town now darkens through sunrise, but it was told to touch one clause and the rest of dawn is still on the night's clock. Two measured leftovers. (1) w.last = span - 0.05 - 0.9*hOn is still keyed on the dawn edge, so the ~5% burn-through windows darken at sunUp+0.7..+1.6 and winter holds a flat 2-3 panes from sunUp+0.4, dropping to 1 only by +1.2: the last lamps in town still go out after sunrise. (2) nightF's curve and daylight's disagree by about an hour — lawn walkers now cross the courtyard at nightF > 0.5, measured at hour 4.95-5.74 with sunrise at 4.01, so there is an hour of real daylight the town still paints as night (shots/b108-dawn-cand.png). Make dawn one event. Sky is seven iterations back and sky x polish is saturated since #32, so this is Deepen: the whole light curve at first light, not a nudge to one constant.
successLooksLike: From sunUp-1 to sunUp+1.5, on a winter day and a summer day, the light on the town and the lamps in the windows tell the same story: it gets lighter, and the lamps go out before or as it does. No pane is lit after sunUp+0.5.
avoid: Do not move NIGHT_K or nightF's edges globally on a hunch — they are read by the evening half, by drawRiverLights, by catA's window and by every spawner that asks whether it is night, and the evening is not broken. Prove containment by canvas hash at pinned instants on both builds (identical outside the dawn band, differing inside it), the way #109 did; the census cannot see a draw-only vector. Remember the day rolls at hour 6.00 and a winter dawn band straddles it.
